newsitem.title: philippines: Philippine call money steady, T-bill rates climb.
newsitem.headline: Philippine call money steady, T-bill rates climb.

text.p: * Central Bank raises special T-bill rates

Philippine overnight money was unchanged at 10.53125 percent, but secondary Treasury bill rates were climbing after the Central Bank raised the interest rate on its special series Treasury bills, traders said.
The Central Bank hiked its 89-day bill rate to 10.673 percent from 10.575 percent, and its 159-day bill rate to 11.0 percent from 10.80 percent.
Traders took the rate adjustment as an indication that the Central Bank was willing to let interest rates rise to stem the steady depreciation of the peso against the dollar.

The peso has been slipping against the U.S. dollar in the past days due to the narrowing interest rate differentials between the two currencies. Accordingly, banks also increased their secondary T-bill rates.
Three-month bills were being bid between 10.69 to 10.90, and being offered between 10.625 and 10.70 percent. On Thursday, most banks were offering their three-month bills at around 10.60 percent.
Six-month bills were being bid between 11.10 to 11.25 percent, while being offered between 11.0 to 11.175 percent, up from the range of 11.0 to 11.125 percent on Thursday.
One-year bills were being bought between 11.35 to 11.675, while being offered between 11.25 to 11.55 percent.
Another trader added that the bank's selling mode could be attributed to the market's anticipation of a slight tightness next week as banks have parked their funds in five-day reverse repos.
In the interbank call loan market, turnover was meagre with only 4.019 billion pesos changing hands. Done rates ranged from 10.53125 to 10.5625 percent.- RAMONCITO DELA CRUZ 63 2 8418938
